$comment: Known environment failures: per platform (process.platform) and backend, the scenario keys that differ for a reason outside the runtime (and, as "perf:<page>" with "bench": true, perf/bench.mjs pages that fail for a recorded reason). run.mjs check reports such a scenario as KNOWN and does not count it as failed only when exactly these keys differ; any other difference fails. Every entry names its reason. Under "*" (every platform), an entry with "notApplicable": true marks a scenario that tests a behavior the backend's engine does not have; any difference is then known.

39-policy-rules.reason: The scenario tests WebKit content-rule compile errors (a pattern that parses but cannot compile). Headless Chromium filters requests through CDP Fetch and compiles no content rules, and the Rust policy refuses "é://example.com" when it is set, so no compile error can occur.

perf:deep-1k.reason: perf/bench.mjs page deep-1k (1000 nested divs): on Chromium the page agent's recursive snapshot walk overflows the renderer stack between DOM depth 700 and 900 (V8 trivial recursion depth 12,480), and a result nested deeper than about 300 levels fails CDP's CBOR conversion. Not the QuickJS VM. Fix (ff, 2026-10-06): explicit-stack walk, flat pre-order node list with depth, iterative rebuild and rendering, after item 4, based on classic's depth bound (round 16) once it lands on main. Constraints (ff): keep classic's 1,000-level depth budget over all stitched frames and its exact cut notes ("nested deeper than 1000 elements; snapshot this ref to read it" in snapshots, "<!-- not read: parts of the page nested deeper than 1000 elements -->" in Markdown) so WebKit and Chromium match; the flat pre-order list stays required on Chromium (CDP CBOR limit about 300 levels); add a parity case at depth 1,200 that checks the cut note on both engines.

05-input.reason: Meta+A is not select-all on Linux (WebKit and Chromium use Ctrl+A there), so the field keeps its text and fires change on blur; the goldens are macOS behavior.

18-print.reason: Linux font metrics render the printed text image 1 px taller (400x38 instead of 400x37).
